tool_args.rationale: The five paid measurements strongly identify an essentially H-independent linear-in-u_now law (slope ~1.86, near-zero intercept). A coarse adiabatic model is the closest supported mechanistic family, but the code must expose fitted parameters from fit to predict; the current interface lacks a way to pass that fit result, so this model implementation is not executable as specified.

considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: The observed values track a simple smooth mechanism: across varied x_now, predictions are near a linear function of u_now, with no residual signs of fast transient or coupled memory; an added trajectory batch is not currently needed.
It is explicitly nuisance/high-variance and provides no identified value for distinguishing the observed smooth response.

considered_alternatives.option: before/after perturbation contrast or static linear law
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Rows vary u_past and H, but response is almost exactly 1.86*u_now - about 0.001, independent of x_now and H; the adiabatic relaxation model can represent this boundary behavior, while contrast models cannot.
All H values cluster around 4.2 and y remains positive and monotone in u_now; no evidence for reversal or sign oscillation.
